title: Long simultaneous EQ ramps across all saturation selectors

eq_schedule.at_each_host_block: queue all listed control points at sample offset 0; values ramp across each selector segment
eq_schedule.low_frequency_normalized: cycles all four choices every 640 frames
eq_schedule.mid_frequency_normalized: cycles all six choices every 320 frames
eq_schedule.high_pass_frequency_normalized: cycles all five choices every 1024 frames
eq_schedule.input: high-drive stereo tones, deterministic noise, and impulses; scale 8

instance_setup: Two target and two port instances receive isolated input blocks; compare corresponding ordinal positions.
limitations: The licensed target returns E_NOINTERFACE from setProcessing(1), but process() renders all frames.

The residual at 44.1 kHz for 128- and 320-frame blocks is concentrated in Mic selectors after transitions from Line; all measured relative RMS residuals remain below −100 dB. Other six rate/block runs are bit-identical.
Automation is block-quantized, with one value point for each parameter per block; it does not test within-block sample-offset automation.
